thread:
Alex R: Quick thought — our per-org caps feel too rigid for bursty workloads (mobile apps doing syncs). What if instead of a strict RPM we expose a smoothing layer + burst credits?
Priya S: +1, curious how you imagine credits working — leak bucket?
Alex R: Similar to leak bucket but on the org-level. We track a smoothedRPM (EWMA over 30s) and a separate burst_credits counter that accrues when smoothedRPM < baseline and depletes on spikes. Credits capped by org tier.
Marco T: Sketch: baseline = committed RPM, smoothing_window=30s, alpha=0.2 for EWMA. burst_capacity = baseline * burst_mult. Metrics: smoothed_rpm, burst_credits, inflight_concurrency.
Dana L: That helps UX too — console can show current credits and predicted depletion at current rate. Ops can nudge thresholds.
Alex R: Example config prototype: ```yaml
rate_policy:
  baseline_rpm: 600
  smoothing_window_s: 30
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
  burst_mult: 2.0
  concurrency_cap: 40
  credit_recharge_rate: 50  # tokens per minute
```
Priya S: We need to be careful about DoS abuse — credits can be gamed if they recharge too fast. Also how does this interact with token-based billing (TPM)?
Marco T: Two-layer enforcement: tokens (TPM) still enforced by token-metering; credits are a soft throttle on request admission for latency-sensitive endpoints. If TPM exceeded, hard reject. Credits only for smoothing request pacing.
Dana L: For telemetry we should emit: org.smoothed_rpm, org.burst_credits, org.credit_recharge_rate, org.concurrency_inflight, org.hard_rejects. That will let SRE tie latency regressions to credit exhaustion.
Alex R: Rollout plan: flag behind feature-flag per org. Start in read-only telemetry mode for 2 weeks (no enforcement), then soft-enforce (slow 429s with header X-Rate-Warning), then hard-enforce after metrics look stable.
Priya S: Console UX idea: when you edit quota in Console, show an estimated 95th pct smoothed_rpm from last 7d and projected credit buffer under that setting. Add "enable burst smoothing" toggle.
Marco T: Edge cases: many small concurrent connections from same org can still spike concurrency even if rpm smoothed. Need a concurrency cap separate from credits. If concurrency cap hit we should prefer queueing for a short TTL rather than immediate reject for dx.
Dana L: Implementation notes for runtime: prefer atomic ops in our routing proxy to update credits per request to avoid race windows. Use single-shot Redis LUA script: decrement credits + increment inflight atomically and return state.
Alex R: infra-bot: deploy plan?
infra-bot: Starting canary rollout to 10% of traffic for org-burst-smoothing-feature flag. Canary window: 48h. Telemetry dashboard created at /dashboards/org-burst-smoothing (owner: eng-platform).
Priya S: For alerts: add alert when org.hard_rejects > 0.5% of requests for >5m and when average credit_recharge_rate deviates >20% from configured.
Marco T: We should also add a debug endpoint that prints the computed smoothed_rpm and credits for an org id for quick support triage. Protect it behind admin auth.
Dana L: Agree. Also add sampling logs for transitions (credits exhausted -> soft reject -> hard reject) for offline investigation.
Alex R: Action items: (1) Marco to write Redis LUA prototype + perf test (2) Dana to add telemetry names and tentative Grafana panels (3) Priya to draft console UI copy + mock for toggle and buffer projection (4) I'll add rollout playbook and alert thresholds.
Priya S: Sounds good. Can we squeeze in a unit test for burst credit math? The corner case where many sequential small requests inflate credits unintentionally worried me.
Marco T: Will add tests and a tiny sim script to validate recharge/consume under multiple traffic shapes.
Dana L: I'll create the dashboard JSON draft and post link once done.
Alex R: Thanks all — moving to a tiny RFC doc later today. If anyone wants to piggyback on the console mocks ping me. :thumbsup:
